descriptions.floors: Floors climbed based on elevation gain detected by your device.
descriptions.active_minutes: Time spent at a moderate or higher activity level.
descriptions.calories_out: Total calories burned including your resting metabolic rate.
descriptions.active_zone_minutes: Minutes spent in fat burn, cardio or peak heart rate zones; cardio and peak count double.
descriptions.moderate_intensity_min: Time at moderate intensity (brisk walking, light cycling). The WHO recommends 150–300 minutes a week.
descriptions.vigorous_intensity_min: Time at high intensity (running, hard effort). Counts double toward weekly activity targets.
descriptions.sleep_duration_min: Total time asleep last night. Adults generally need 7–9 hours.
descriptions.sleep_deep_min: Deep (slow-wave) sleep, the most restorative stage. Critical for physical recovery and immune function.
descriptions.sleep_light_min: The transition between wakefulness and deeper stages; most of a sleep cycle.
descriptions.sleep_rem_min: REM sleep supports memory, learning and emotional regulation. It grows in later cycles.
descriptions.sleep_wake_min: Time awake or restless during the night. Brief awakenings are normal.
descriptions.sleep_efficiency: Share of the time in bed actually spent asleep. Above 85 % is generally good.
descriptions.sleep_score: Overall sleep quality out of 100: duration, stage balance, SpO2 and HRV.
descriptions.sleep_time_to_fall_asleep_min: How long it took to settle into deep sleep after first falling asleep. Lower is generally better.
descriptions.sleep_sound_sleep_min: Longest stretch of uninterrupted sleep. An approximation of Fitbit's metric, which also uses motion data.
descriptions.sleep_restlessness_min: Brief stirring during the night: awake phases under 5 minutes. An approximation of Fitbit's metric.
descriptions.sleep_interruptions_min: Awake phases of 5 minutes or longer that you're likely to remember.
descriptions.sleep_full_awakenings: Number of wake events of 5 minutes or longer.
descriptions.resting_hr: Heart rate at full rest. A downward trend reflects improving fitness.
descriptions.avg_heart_rate: Average heart rate across the day. Rises with activity, stress and fever.
descriptions.spo2_avg: Blood oxygen saturation overnight. Typically 95–100 %; dips below 90 % may point to sleep apnea.
descriptions.respiratory_rate: Breaths per minute during sleep, normally 12–20. Elevated values may signal illness or stress.
descriptions.hrv_daily_rmssd: Variation between heartbeats. Higher values mean better recovery.
descriptions.skin_temp_variation: Nightly skin temperature against your baseline. Elevated readings can indicate illness or hormonal changes.
descriptions.vo2_max: Estimated VO₂ max, often given as a range. A key indicator of long-term heart health.
descriptions.max_hr: Highest heart rate recorded during the day.
descriptions.weight_kg: Current body weight from your scale.
descriptions.body_fat_pct: Fat as a share of body weight. Healthy ranges vary by age and sex.
descriptions.bone_mass_kg: Estimated bone mineral content. Stable values are normal.
descriptions.body_water_pct: Water as a share of weight, normally 45–65 %.
descriptions.lean_mass_kg: Everything except fat: muscle, bone, organs and water.
descriptions.fat_mass_kg: Total fat tissue. The trend says more than a single reading.
descriptions.visceral_fat: Fat around the organs. Higher levels raise metabolic and heart risk.
descriptions.visceral_fat_index: Rating of visceral fat; below 13 is generally healthy.
descriptions.extracellular_water_kg: Water outside cells. Elevated levels may point to inflammation or fluid retention.
descriptions.intracellular_water_kg: Water inside cells; reflects hydration at the cellular level.
descriptions.vascular_age: Estimated age of your arteries from pulse wave velocity.
descriptions.metabolic_age: Your metabolism compared with age norms.
descriptions.basal_metabolic_rate: Energy your body uses at complete rest over 24 hours.
descriptions.nerve_health_score: Monthly score from your Withings scale, from daily EDA readings. Above 50 is normal.
descriptions.eda_feet: Daily electrodermal activity of your feet; feeds the nerve health score.
descriptions.pulse_wave_velocity: Speed of the pulse along the arteries. Lower means more elastic vessels.
descriptions.ecg_heart_rate: Heart rate measured during an ECG on your scale.
descriptions.ecg_afib: Atrial fibrillation screening of the ECG. “Normal” means no irregular rhythm in this reading.
descriptions.body_battery_high: Highest Body Battery today (0–100). Charges with rest and sleep.
descriptions.body_battery_low: Lowest Body Battery today. Below 20 your body may need rest.
descriptions.stress_avg: Average Garmin stress level (0–100). Lower is calmer.

earlyBird.label: Early bird
earlyBird.text: You naturally wake early and feel most energized in the morning. Mornings are your prime time.

morning.label: Morning type
morning.text: You do your best work in the first half of the day and tend to wake up refreshed. Most schedules suit you well.

intermediate.label: Intermediate
intermediate.text: Your body clock fits typical schedules; you adapt easily between early mornings and late evenings.

evening.label: Evening type
evening.text: You come alive in the afternoon and evening. Mornings can be a challenge.

nightOwl.label: Night owl
nightOwl.text: Your body clock runs late. You're sharpest in the evening and may struggle with early alarms.

readiness.title: Daily readiness
readiness.calibrating: Calibrating… {{days}} of {{needed}} nights with HRV data
readiness.calibratingText: Needs {{needed}} nights in which your device recorded HRV during sleep. A snug fit helps.
readiness.baselineWithRhr: HRV baseline {{hrv}} ms · resting HR baseline {{rhr}} bpm
readiness.accuracy_one: Based on {{count}} day; accuracy improves as more data comes in.
readiness.accuracy_other: Based on {{count}} days; accuracy improves as more data comes in.

leads.solid: Solid recovery: you can train normally.
leads.moderate: Moderate recovery: go lighter than usual today.
leads.low: Recovery is low. Treat this as a deload day.

drivers.penalty: Yesterday's activity load is the main drag (penalty −{{penalty}}): your body is still paying back a hard effort.
drivers.hrvLow: Your HRV ({{today}} ms) is well below your {{baseline}} ms baseline: recovery comes first. Drink, eat enough and put sleep first tonight.
drivers.hrvBelow: HRV ({{today}} ms) is below your {{baseline}} ms baseline, the main signal here. Light activity helps more than a hard session.
drivers.rhrHigh: Resting HR is elevated ({{today}} vs a baseline of {{baseline}}): a possible early sign of illness or too little recovery.
drivers.rhrUp: Resting HR ({{today}}) is up from your {{baseline}} baseline. Watch for signs of illness and keep intensity in check.
drivers.sleepLow: Last night's sleep ({{score}}) is dragging this down. Skip caffeine after noon and go to bed earlier.
drivers.sleepWeak: Sleep ({{score}}) is the weakest signal today. An earlier bedtime tonight pays off tomorrow.
drivers.allStrong: Every part is strong. A good day for harder training or a personal record.
drivers.allHealthy: All signals are healthy: train as planned.
drivers.cumulative: The parts look fine on their own, likely fatigue built up over the week. A lighter session still makes sense.

optimal.label: Optimal
optimal.text: Your body shows strong recovery and balance. A great day for what matters to you.

balanced.label: Balanced
balanced.text: Your body is steady today. A good day to keep your routine.

low.label: Low
low.text: Your body is asking for a bit more rest. Taking it easier helps you recharge.
